judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 25% factor applied to a stated premium base, with a listed automobile load; only the external manual reference is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The private passenger load is $80 here but $50 in the Nursing Home section (c088) — different rating sections, so not necessarily inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise rate-per-$1,000-receipts ladder; the only softness is what counts as an 'Imaging (MRI) risk'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with the excess factors in c096 and the automobile cross-reference to c093; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Caps credits at 25% but leaves debits unlimited and discretion unqualified; otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says 'at OHIC's discretion' where the parallel nursing home provision (c089) says 'at the REINSURED'S discretion' — the same party under Amendment No. 3 (c068).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean ladder of percentages applied to 'the modified First Million price'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the First Million definition in c093 and the credit rule in c095.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The first million is subject to a minimum premium of $1,500,000' states a minimum premium exceeding the layer of cover it prices — an evident mechanical error that changes the meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VI (c018) makes premium subject to 'the applicable minimum premium specified in the Rating Schedule', so the erroneous figure has operative bite, and it does not track the Nursing Home minimums in c091.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The factor is given as '-is' (unreadable) with a charge of 25, so the entry cannot be applied as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs from the Hospital and Nursing Home versions of the same factor (c084, c092) without explanation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Termination 'with respect to loss under policies issued on or after January 1, 1998' keys the cut-off to issuance, whereas the agreement elsewhere speaks of policies 'becoming effective' or 'in force', and it does not say what happens to earlier policies' run-off.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article XI (c033) already prescribes a run-off on cancellation ('all policies in force ... until their individual natural expiration or next anniversary ... 12 months plus odd time'), and Article VII (c025) defers contingent commission past termination, so the three must be read together to fix the parties' continuing obligations.
